I. GENERAL
In essence, Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children constitute a form of social discrimination, violation of human rights, and a crime against human dignity. The issue of Gender-Based Violence needs to receive serious attention, therefore the state has issued Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, which can serve as a foundation in creating a social and state life encompassed by peace, equality, and gender-based social justice.
Law Number 23 of 2004 has stated that all forms of Violence within the scope of the household, whether affecting one of the partners (husband/wife) or family members (especially children) constitute a violation of human rights and a crime against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination that must be eliminated, so that the state and/or society must prevent and are obligated to fulfill the rights of every citizen to obtain Protection in order to avoid and be free from Violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.
Discriminatory treatment and Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children in Salatiga City can potentially reduce the quality of family and community life, thus requiring integrated handling. The Salatiga City Government carefully captures the issue of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children and subsequently implements Regional development programs based on the spirit of strengthening opportunity, equality, and Gender-Based social justice as outlined in the Salatiga City Medium-Term Development Plan for 2011-2016. Nevertheless, in line with community aspirations, the Salatiga City Government deems it necessary to increase attention, response, and action in handling these issues.
In relation to this matter, the Salatiga City Government together with the Salatiga City Regional House of Representatives need to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively that is beneficial for providing understanding, knowledge, and education regarding various forms of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children as well as to provide legal certainty to Victims regarding where they should seek Protection.
This Regional Regulation is also intended to provide understanding and instill the value that every citizen without exception has the right to obtain a sense of security and be free from all forms of Violence, whether occurring within the scope of the household (family) or the scope of society.

Article 6
Every Victim of Gender-Based Violence and Children has the obligation to:
a. provide truthful and accountable information to interested parties; and
b. be willing to become a witness if it does not endanger oneself and obtain security guarantees.

Article 9
In the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, the community, family, and parents have the obligation and responsibility to:
a. prevent the occurrence of Violence incidents;
b. provide information and report Violence incidents to the relevant parties; and
c. participate in the handling of Violence Victims.

1.2.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation clearly covers sexual violence within its scope/definitions. Pasal 1 angka 7 defines “Kekerasan” as causing suffering “baik fisik, seksual, psikologis…”, and Pasal 1 angka 9 defines “Kekerasan Berbasis Gender” as causing suffering “secara fisik, seksual, ekonomi, sosial, psikis…”. Also Pasal 1 angka 11 (kekerasan terhadap anak) includes “kekerasan fisik, seksual, psikologis…”. These are explicit mentions of sexual violence (kekerasan seksual). The retrieved English candidates actually contained this (e.g., [2.3-4]/[6.5-4] include “physical, sexual, psychological”), so a correct judge could answer Yes. I. GENERAL
In essence, Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children constitute a form of social discrimination, violation of human rights, and a crime against human dignity. The issue of Gender-Based Violence needs to receive serious attention, therefore the state has issued Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence and Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, which can serve as a foundation in creating a social and state life encompassed by peace, equality, and gender-based social justice.
Law Number 23 of 2004 has stated that all forms of Violence within the scope of the household, whether affecting one of the partners (husband/wife) or family members (especially children) constitute a violation of human rights and a crime against human dignity as well as a form of discrimination that must be eliminated, so that the state and/or society must prevent and are obligated to fulfill the rights of every citizen to obtain Protection in order to avoid and be free from Violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth.
Discriminatory treatment and Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children in Salatiga City can potentially reduce the quality of family and community life, thus requiring integrated handling. The Salatiga City Government carefully captures the issue of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children and subsequently implements Regional development programs based on the spirit of strengthening opportunity, equality, and Gender-Based social justice as outlined in the Salatiga City Medium-Term Development Plan for 2011-2016. Nevertheless, in line with community aspirations, the Salatiga City Government deems it necessary to increase attention, response, and action in handling these issues.
In relation to this matter, the Salatiga City Government together with the Salatiga City Regional House of Representatives need to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively that is beneficial for providing understanding, knowledge, and education regarding various forms of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children as well as to provide legal certainty to Victims regarding where they should seek Protection.
This Regional Regulation is also intended to provide understanding and instill the value that every citizen without exception has the right to obtain a sense of security and be free from all forms of Violence, whether occurring within the scope of the household (family) or the scope of society.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is the City of Salatiga.
7. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any act based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life, including domestic violence.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Salatiga.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit within the Regional Government that carries out certain regional government affairs based on the principles of autonomy and assistance duties.
5. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of Victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
6. Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of Violence, case handling and post-crisis handling, coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation.
10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb as referred to in Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.
11. Violence against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion, and all forms of treatment carried out against children that results in and is not limited to physical, sexual, psychological violence, economic exploitation, including neglect and maltreatment that degrades the dignity of the Child.
12. Complaint is notification regarding an incident of violence either in writing or orally by the Victim or other parties to interested parties.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, as well as interpreters for the purpose of self-empowerment of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children to resolve the problems they face.
15. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and Victims that supports the reunification of Victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide Protection and fulfillment of the needs of Victims.
16. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide Protection to Victims.

6.5.rationale: The original Indonesian text includes disability/condition explicitly within its non-discrimination principle explanation. In the Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf a, non-discrimination is defined as protection for all victims without distinguishing, among other things, “kondisi fisik dan mental.” This is an explicit inclusion of physical/mental condition (commonly used to cover disability). The retrieved English candidate [6.5-36] contains the same phrase (“physical and mental condition”). Therefore, if the indicator is about whether the policy addresses disability as an intersectional category (not necessarily providing special measures), the correct answer is Yes and the golden label is consistent; the judge’s No reflects an overly narrow requirement for ‘special targeted measures’ rather than explicit inclusion under non-discrimination.

6.7.evaluator_rationale: The non-discrimination principle lists characteristics such as ethnicity, religion, race, culture, and language, but the candidate sentences do not provide special protection measures targeted specifically at women from minority or isolated groups; they only provide general protections without group-specific measures.

6.7.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes minority-related characteristics under the non-discrimination principle. In the Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf a, non-discrimination covers victims without distinguishing “suku, agama, ras, golongan, … etnis, budaya dan bahasa …”. These are classic minority-group markers (ethnicity/tribe, religion, race, culture, language). The retrieved English candidate [6.7-36] contains these categories. Thus, if the indicator asks whether minority groups are addressed/included, the policy does so via explicit non-discrimination coverage. The judge’s No again seems to require special targeted measures, which is not necessary to satisfy an ‘inclusion of minority groups’ indicator; therefore the golden label Yes appears correct and the judge decision is the problem.
